sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitter Nate Cheeseman, SIL; supporter Ethnologue Editor). 2016. Change Request Number 2016-005: Retire [rie] Rien — adopted, effective 2017-01-31. Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress or any linguistic feature. p.2, section 3(a): reason for retirement 'There is no evidence that the language exists.' 3(c): 'The name for this purported language apparently came from the 1954 listing from David Thomas. Most linguists working in Southeast Asia have not heard of this language. The Ethnologue seems to be the sole source of information on this group. Perhaps David Thomas confused Rien [rie] with the Eastern Bru [bru] dialect called Leun or Leung.. More likely.. a village name. The only reference for Rien [rie] in Glottolog 2.6 is Schliesinger (2003). However,…
Nothing. Page marks the entry as retired/bookkeeping, reason 'non-existent', effective 2017-01-31, CR 2016-005; no bibliographic references listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
Nothing. Status 'Deprecated' 2017-01-31 via CR 2016-005; scope individual, type living (historical metadata).
